items.title: Strait of Hormuz area (Bandar Abbas vicinity), Iran: European countries may face drug shortages as the Strait of Hormuz disruption threatens supplies of essential goods; about 80% of Europe's pharmaceutical supply chain depends on China and India, both affected by higher energy prices.
items.description: European countries may face drug shortages as the Strait of Hormuz disruption threatens supplies of essential goods; about 80% of Europe's pharmaceutical supply chain depends on China and India, both affected by higher energy prices.
items.rawSummary: Iranian plans to implement a fee-and-traffic management mechanism for the Strait of Hormuz have emerged as the waterway remains virtually closed to merchant shipping, with only a handful of vessels transiting under Iranian protocols while U.S. naval forces interdict Iran-linked traffic and diplomatic efforts seek an end to the crisis.
items.analysis: Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has all but ceased, with fewer than five vessels transiting daily compared to a pre-war average of 130, as Iran asserts territorial sovereignty and enforces a selective transit protocol. Iran has now announced it will soon unveil a 'professional mechanism' to formalize traffic management and fee collection, reserving passage for commercial and cooperating vessels while barring those linked to the U.S.-led 'Project Freedom'. U.S. CENTCOM has interdicted 79 Iran-linked vessels, effectively shutting the strait from both ends and suppressing Iran's fast-boat activity. U.S.-China talks produced shared opposition to tolls and militarization, but China has not explicitly rejected Iranian sovereignty claims, and concerns linger over potential Chinese arms sales to Iran. The prolonged disruption is raising fears of drug shortages in Europe and threatening supplies of essential goods reliant on Asia-based supply chains.

items.rawSummary: U.S. and Israeli military officials are reportedly preparing targets for possible strikes on Iran that could begin as early as next week, amid ongoing diplomatic pressure and conflicting intelligence about Iran's military capabilities.
items.analysis: CNN reported that U.S. and Israeli military officials are preparing targets for potential strikes on Iran that could begin as early as next week, echoing earlier reports from The New York Times. The Times had detailed planning beyond airstrikes to include special forces deployments to Isfahan and Kharg Island to seize enriched uranium. These preparations follow President Trump's return from China and his warnings that the U.S. would bomb nuclear facilities or 'go in' if nuclear material is not secured. Conflicting assessments persist, with U.S. intelligence indicating Iran retains roughly 70% of its missile stockpile and the majority of its Strait of Hormuz positions, while CENTCOM's commander claims Iran's command-and-control is collapsing. China is reportedly applying significant economic pressure on Iran to reach a nuclear agreement, and Iran's inability to export oil by sea for nearly a month underscores its deepening isolation.

items.title: United States (Diplomatic focus on Iran), United States: Former National Security Advisor Jake Sullivan stated the U.S. is in an active shooting war with Iran that he called a war of choice, questioning its purpose and the absence of an imminent threat.
items.description: Former National Security Advisor Jake Sullivan stated the U.S. is in an active shooting war with Iran that he called a war of choice, questioning its purpose and the absence of an imminent threat.
items.rawSummary: The United States is involved in an active military conflict with Iran while facing domestic economic headwinds and political scrutiny over the war's justification, alongside ongoing diplomatic strains over trade, technology, and Taiwan.
items.analysis: Hostilities between the U.S. and Iran have escalated into an active shooting war, former National Security Advisor Jake Sullivan stated, calling it a war of choice and questioning its rationale in the absence of an imminent threat. President Trump accused Iran of reneging on five nuclear deals and claimed he held back a final military operation at Pakistan's request. Iranian officials continue to demand recognized control over the Strait of Hormuz as a guarantee against U.S.-Israeli attacks, and China has not committed to freedom-of-navigation operations. Separately, House Speaker Mike Johnson defended congressional stock trading by pointing to lawmakers' frozen salaries, as the median salary remains $174,000 and many Americans lack emergency savings; his remarks follow CNBC's report that Trump purchased Palantir Technologies stock before promoting the company. Trump also described Taiwan as a difficult problem given its proximity to China and stated the U.S. leads China in artificial intelligence, while Secretary Rubio cautioned against selling cutting-edge chips to China to maintain technological dominance. Domestic pressures accumulate with over 100 vacant ambassador posts, Jerome Powell's departure as Federal Reserve chair, and full-time employment falling by 424,000 in April, bringing the year-to-date decline to 963,000.

items.rawSummary: As U.S.-led negotiations remain stalled over Iran’s demand for security guarantees, tensions persist with Tehran asserting control over the Strait of Hormuz and both sides signaling military readiness, while domestic civil defense efforts intensify.
items.analysis: Senior Iranian officials continue to demand guarantees against future U.S. and Israeli attacks as a precondition for negotiations, and Tehran appears to view recognized control over the Strait of Hormuz as one such guarantee. Foreign Minister Araghchi has insisted Iran restricts strait passage only for adversaries and is in talks with Oman on joint management, while Al Jazeera reported that Washington rejected all conditions. Regionally, China remains noncommittal on U.S.-led freedom of navigation, the UAE is accelerating a port bypass at Fujairah, and Saudi Arabia is reportedly weighing a non-aggression pact with Iran. Domestically, the confirmation of General Mousavi’s death after weeks of recovery efforts underscored severe leadership losses, and state television has now aired footage of an IRGC instructor teaching civilians basic rifle use, likely a sign of stepped-up public defense preparations. Meanwhile, the New York Times cited officials saying the U.S. and Israel are preparing possible renewed combat as early as next week, including strikes and a special forces uranium extraction mission, while former President Trump claimed the U.S. could disable Iran’s bridges and electricity in two days and said a quick military win would boost Republican electoral prospects.

items.rawSummary: Ukrainian decoy drone crashes in Samsun, Turkey, causing damage to buildings.
items.analysis: A Ukrainian 'Maya' decoy drone crashed in the Turkish coastal city of Samsun, damaging rooftops and windows. The drone likely lost its course during a mission toward Crimea or Russia's Krasnodar region, possibly due to malfunction or Russian electronic jamming. The incident adds to previous occurrences of stray drones entering Turkish territory, including Russian reconnaissance models. No casualties were reported, but the crash highlights the spillover risks from the war for NATO members on the Black Sea.

items.rawSummary: As U.S.-led negotiations remain stalled over Iran’s demand for security guarantees, tensions persist with Tehran asserting control over the Strait of Hormuz and both sides signaling military readiness, while domestic civil defense efforts intensify.
items.analysis: Senior Iranian officials continue to demand guarantees against future U.S. and Israeli attacks as a precondition for negotiations, and Tehran appears to view recognized control over the Strait of Hormuz as one such guarantee. Foreign Minister Araghchi has insisted Iran restricts strait passage only for adversaries and is in talks with Oman on joint management, while Al Jazeera reported that Washington rejected all conditions. Regionally, China remains noncommittal on U.S.-led freedom of navigation, the UAE is accelerating a port bypass at Fujairah, and Saudi Arabia is reportedly weighing a non-aggression pact with Iran. Domestically, the confirmation of General Mousavi’s death after weeks of recovery efforts underscored severe leadership losses, and state television has now aired footage of an IRGC instructor teaching civilians basic rifle use, likely a sign of stepped-up public defense preparations. Meanwhile, the New York Times cited officials saying the U.S. and Israel are preparing possible renewed combat as early as next week, including strikes and a special forces uranium extraction mission, while former President Trump claimed the U.S. could disable Iran’s bridges and electricity in two days and said a quick military win would boost Republican electoral prospects.

items.title: Iranian regime governmental centers (unspecified locations), Iran: The son of Iranian Armed Forces General Staff head Abdolrahim Mousavi revealed that his father’s body was buried under rubble for nearly 30 days after he was killed on the first day of U.S. and Israeli strikes targeting Khamenei’s office; Mousavi had only recently been appointed after his predecessor was killed in a 12-day war.

items.title: Southern Lebanon (Klaouieh, Arzoun, Nabatieh al-Fawqa), Lebanon: Lebanon and Israel extended their ceasefire by 45 days.
items.description: Lebanon and Israel extended their ceasefire by 45 days.
items.rawSummary: Clashes persisted in southern Lebanon with Israeli strikes and drone interceptions, but Lebanon and Israel later agreed to a 45-day ceasefire extension.
items.analysis: Military activity continued across southern Lebanon on May 15, with the IDF intercepting one drone and reporting several others landing in open areas, describing it as another Hezbollah ceasefire violation. This followed a series of heavy exchanges that included a Hezbollah drone wounding three civilians near Rosh Hanikra on May 14 and the killing of over 20 operatives in Israeli strikes. Hezbollah has maintained drone operations, damaging an Israeli armored bulldozer near Naqoura and a UNIFIL base. The IDF expanded counter-drone measures, distributing 158,000 square meters of anti-explosive-drone netting and ordering more, reflecting the persistent threat. Despite these ongoing hostilities and heavy activity reported in northern Israel, Lebanon and Israel announced a 45-day extension of their ceasefire later on May 15, suggesting continued diplomatic efforts to manage the volatile situation.
items.keyPoint: Lebanon and Israel extended their ceasefire by 45 days.
